summary: Low risk. No critical vulnerabilities. Strong cryptography, XSS protection, path traversal guards, and secrets management. One low-severity input validation gap identified.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing input validation on per_page parameter
vulnerabilities.description: The 'per_page' query parameter is converted to int() without bounds checking or error handling. Sending ?per_page=abc causes ValueError and crashes the request handler thread, resulting in a 500 error.
vulnerabilities.impact: Request-level denial-of-service (single request fails with 500 error). Mitigated by authentication requirement and request-level isolation.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Wrap conversion in try-except block with sensible default fallback (e.g., per=5). Validate range: per = max(1, min(100, int(per)))

strengths.finding: Uses scrypt(n=2¹⁴, r=8, p=1) with hmac.compare_digest() for constant-time password verification. No weak hashing (MD5/SHA1).
Cookies configured with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Lax flags. Session tokens generated via secrets.token_urlsafe(32).
All file operations use Path.resolve() + is_relative_to() to enforce directory bounds. No traversal risk detected.
User input consistently escaped with H.escHtml() before HTML insertion. SVG colors sourced from hardcoded zone arrays, not user input.
All subprocess calls use array form (no shell=True). No string interpolation in command arguments.
No hardcoded credentials in code. Garmin passwords not logged or persisted. Environment variables secured in deployment config (0600 file permissions).
API keys stored only in sessionStorage (browser memory, cleared on session close). Never persisted to disk or localStorage.
HTTP body size capped at 1 MiB on unauthenticated login endpoint to prevent memory exhaustion attacks.
Numeric fields (RPE, FTP, W', bike profile values) validated with range checks before persistence.

non_issues: SQL injection — No SQL queries in codebase (file-based JSON storage only)
XML External Entity (XXE) — Custom XML parser has no external entity support; safe for untrusted ZWO/ERG/MRC workout files
Unescaped XSS — All user input escaped before rendering
ReDoS patterns — No dangerous regex detected
Credential leakage — Passwords/tokens not logged or exposed in error messages

recommendations.action: Fix per_page input validation in scripts/runner.py:887
Add a Content-Security-Policy header in Caddy config for defense-in-depth against XSS
recommendations.impact: Blocks inline scripts even if escaping fails; reduces XSS surface area

recommendations.action: Implement rate limiting per IP for failed login attempts (currently thread-lock only)
recommendations.impact: Hardens brute-force defense; current lock is per-process, not per-IP

recommendations.action: Validate XML parsing limits in workouts.js (max file size, max elements)
recommendations.impact: Prevents malformed ZWO files from causing DoS via resource exhaustion

recommendations.action: Add CORS headers explicitly (allow same-origin only) in Caddy config
recommendations.impact: Defense-in-depth; prevents accidental cross-origin data exposure

assumptions: Environment variables are secured in deployment (~/.config/paceforge/env with 0600 permissions)
Caddy reverse proxy properly enforces authentication before /paceforge/* routes
Localhost (127.0.0.1) is trusted for internal runner port (8223)
Browser environment upstream is XSS-free (e.g., no malicious browser extensions)
Third-party dependencies (urllib3, etc.) are kept current via regular updates
Garmin credentials not persisted; token refresh handled safely per CLAUDE.md
methodology: Source code review across Python (runner.py, actions.py) and JavaScript (web/bike/*.js, web/index.html)
Focus on authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets handling, and injection risks
Comparison against OWASP Top 10 and CWE-25 most dangerous software weaknesses
Review of CLAUDE.md security architecture notes and prior audit findings
